intro: To update Photoshop on a Mac, open the Creative Cloud desktop app from the menu bar, choose Updates, and click Update next to Photoshop. When the button changes to Open, the update is installed, and Photoshop > About Photoshop shows the new version number.
tldr: Photoshop updates come from the Creative Cloud desktop app, not from a Photoshop settings page.
Save your files, quit Photoshop, then click the Creative Cloud icon in the menu bar.
Choose Updates, click Update next to Photoshop, and wait until the button changes to Open.
Confirm the result with Photoshop > About Photoshop. The latest build in this guide is 27.11.
Photoshop 27.8 and 27.11 need macOS 14.0 or later. Check your macOS version first.

blocks.text: Photoshop updates arrive through the Creative Cloud desktop app. That app installs, tracks, and updates the Adobe programs on your Mac, and Photoshop is one of them. The Creative Cloud app knows which builds are available for your account. That is why this guide starts there, not inside Photoshop's own settings.
Two ways to reach the Photoshop update list

The first route starts inside Photoshop. Open the Help menu and choose Updates. That opens the Creative Cloud app on its Updates list. The second route starts in the menu bar. Click the Creative Cloud icon at the upper right of your screen, then choose Updates in the left column. The menu bar route works even when Photoshop is closed, which is the state you want before an install.

Guides do not agree on the labels. Some say Updates, and others say the list sits under an Apps tab. Adobe's own help pages were not available for this guide, so the labels here come from third-party tutorials. Read the labels on your screen and follow what you see. The steps still hold.
Back up presets, brushes and actions before you update

Updates usually keep your custom work. A backup still costs little, and it gives you a way back if a new build changes how something behaves. PhotoshopCAFE recommends exporting three kinds of files before you update. Put them in one new folder, such as a folder in Documents, so you can find them later.

items: Presets: choose Edit > Presets > Export Presets, then save the file.
Brushes: open the gear icon on the Brushes panel, then choose Export Selected Brushes.
Actions: open the flyout menu on the Actions panel, then choose Save Actions.

blocks.text: Select the brushes before you export them. The export covers only the brushes you pick. Keep the backup files outside the Photoshop application folder, so you never have to search inside an app bundle for them.
Check your macOS version before you update

Photoshop 27.8 and 27.11 both require macOS 14.0 or later. CGChannel lists this requirement for each release. If your Mac runs an older system, you cannot install these builds. In that case, stay on an older Photoshop build that matches your system.

To check your macOS version, click the Apple menu, then choose About This Mac. The macOS version appears in the window. Write it down before you start the update. If it reads 14.0 or later, you can install the newest builds.

blocks.text: Treat older guides with care. One guide from August 2024 calls 25.9.1 the current release. An Apple Community reply cites 26.10 as the release that works on macOS 26. Adobe's online documentation calls 27.11 the September 2026 release, while CGChannel dates it October 6, 2026. The date on your screen may differ from both.
Auto-update Photoshop on Mac: settings explained

If you want Photoshop to update without your help, turn on auto-update. Open the Creative Cloud menu, then choose Preferences > Apps. Turn on Auto-update, then turn on the Photoshop option. Click Advanced options to see the choices that matter.

In Advanced options, check Import previous settings and preferences. Leave Remove older versions unchecked. That keeps the previous version on your Mac, so you can fall back to it if a new build misbehaves. Photoshop Essentials describes both settings in its guide.

Auto-update suits people who want new builds without a routine. It fits poorly if a plugin you rely on has not been updated for the newest Photoshop. In that case, leave auto-update off, check the plugin maker's notes, and update on your own schedule.
What changed in the latest Photoshop builds

Adobe's product page lists a newly improved Remove Tool. It also lists two new adjustment layers, Clarity & Dehaze and Grain. The page does not say which build added each one. Read the release notes for your version before you depend on them.

The 27.11 build adds Enhance Edge. CGChannel says each use of Enhance Edge costs 20 generative credits. If your plan has a credit allowance, check your balance before you run it on a large batch of files.

blocks.title: Close Photoshop first
blocks.text: A Conflict Updating Photoshop message means Photoshop or Adobe Bridge is still running. Click Cancel, save your files, quit both apps, then start the update again.
Going back to an older Photoshop build

Some guides describe a way to install an earlier build. PhotoshopCAFE says to click the three-dot button to the left of Open, then choose Other Versions. Its screenshots date from June 2020, so the menu on your Mac may look different today.

The safer path is to keep the old build from the start. Leave Remove older versions unchecked under Advanced options. Then the previous version stays on your Mac, and you have something to switch back to if the new build causes trouble.
Edge cases after a macOS upgrade

One Apple Community thread began with a user on macOS 26.0. That user said Photoshop 2020 stopped working after an upgrade to macOS Tahoe. A top reply said to update through the Creative Cloud app, and that the current release, v26.10, works on macOS 26. Another reply suggested the user meant Photoshop Elements 2020.

If Photoshop stops after a macOS upgrade, check the app name and version first. Then update through Creative Cloud rather than reinstalling from an old disk image. The thread shows that a wrong app name can send you down the wrong path.
Mistakes people make when updating Photoshop

items: Quitting without saving. Save every open file before you start the update.
Clicking Open before the install finishes. Wait for the button to change first.
Following an old guide that names an old build as the latest release.
Skipping the macOS check and finding out only when the install fails.
Deleting Creative Cloud to fix an update. Start with the Updates list instead.

blocks.text: Photoshop on the web is a different product

This guide covers the desktop app for Mac. Photoshop on the web runs in a browser, and this guide does not cover it. The web review this guide found is from a 2022 beta, so its browser list may be out of date. Check Adobe's current web requirements before you rely on that version.
After the update: what to check first

Open a file you use every day and test the tools you rely on. If a tool such as Object Selection is missing from the toolbar, click and hold the three-dot button at the bottom of the toolbar. Choose Restore Defaults, then click Done.

If Photoshop behaves oddly after an update, the settings file may be the cause. A preferences reset clears that file. Export your presets first, then read [how to reset preferences in Photoshop on Mac](/how-to/reset-preferences-in-photoshop). After that, confirm the build with [how to check your Photoshop version in Photoshop on Mac](/how-to/check-your-photoshop-version-in-photoshop).
Where guides disagree, and what to trust

None of the sources in this guide lists a keyboard shortcut for checking for updates. The only related shortcut is for resetting preferences at launch. That is a different task, so do not use it to update.

Trust the steps that match what you see on your screen. Trust version numbers from Adobe or CGChannel over older blogs. Keep a note of the date on every guide you read, because Photoshop changes its menus between builds.

faq.question: Can I update Photoshop from inside Photoshop?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the Help menu and choose Updates. That opens the Updates list in the Creative Cloud app. The menu bar icon reaches the same list, and it works with Photoshop closed.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to update Photoshop on a Mac?
faq.answer: None of the sources in this guide lists one. The shortcuts that matter here are ⌘S to save and ⌘Q to quit before you start the update.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Photoshop 27.11 need?
faq.answer: macOS 14.0 or later. CGChannel lists that requirement for Photoshop 27.11, and the same requirement for 27.8. Check your version from the Apple menu, then About This Mac.

faq.question: Why does my update say Conflict Updating Photoshop?
faq.answer: Photoshop or Adobe Bridge is still open. Click Cancel, save your files, quit both apps, then start the update again.

faq.question: Can I keep the old version after I update?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave Remove older versions unchecked under Advanced options in Creative Cloud > Preferences > Apps. The previous build then stays on your Mac.

faq.question: Will an update delete my presets or brushes?
faq.answer: The sources here do not say that updates delete them. Export your presets, brushes and actions first anyway, as PhotoshopCAFE recommends. It takes little time and gives you a copy.

faq.question: How often does Adobe release a major Photoshop update?
faq.answer: Fix the Photo says Adobe releases major Photoshop updates every six months or so. In the sources here, 27.8 arrived on June 18, 2026, and 27.11 on October 6, 2026.

faq.question: Does this guide work for Photoshop on the web?
faq.answer: No. This guide covers the desktop app for Mac. The web version runs in a browser with its own requirements, so check Adobe's current details before you use it.

steps.name: Save your work and quit Photoshop
steps.text: Save every open file with ⌘S. Then choose Photoshop > Quit Photoshop, or press ⌘Q. Close Adobe Bridge too if it is open, since it can block the update.
steps.tip: A Conflict Updating Photoshop message means something is still running. Click Cancel and start from this step.

steps.name: Click the Creative Cloud icon in the menu bar
steps.text: Look at the upper right of the Mac menu bar. Click the Creative Cloud icon. If you cannot see it, open the Creative Cloud app from your Applications folder.
menuPath: Creative Cloud icon in menu bar
steps.tip: Some guides start from Help > Updates inside Photoshop. That route leads to the same update list.

steps.name: Choose Updates in the left column
steps.text: In the Creative Cloud window, click Updates in the left column. Some guides call this an Apps tab. Use whichever label matches your screen.
steps.tip: If you see a Check for updates link at the top right, click it to refresh the list.

steps.name: Click Update next to Photoshop
steps.text: Find Photoshop in the list of new updates. Click the Update button beside it. The download and install start right after the click.
steps.tip: Keep the Mac awake, and plug in a laptop, until the install finishes.

steps.name: Wait until the button changes to Open
steps.text: The install takes a few minutes. When it finishes, the Update button changes to Open. That means Photoshop is installed and ready to launch.
steps.tip: If the button never changes, read the Creative Cloud window for an error message before you retry.

steps.name: Confirm the new version
steps.text: Click Open, or launch Photoshop from the Dock. Choose Photoshop > About Photoshop and read the version in the window. Compare it with the build you expected.
steps.tip: The latest build in this guide is 27.11. A lower number means the update did not finish.

steps.name: Turn on auto-update if you want it
steps.text: Open the Creative Cloud menu, then choose Preferences > Apps. Turn on Auto-update and the Photoshop option. Click Advanced options and leave Remove older versions unchecked.
steps.tip: Skip this step if a plugin you use has not been updated for the newest build.

shortcuts.action: Reset preferences at launch, only if needed

troubleshooting.fix: Click Cancel. Save your files, quit Photoshop, close Adobe Bridge, then retry the update from the Updates list.

troubleshooting.problem: The Update button does not appear
troubleshooting.fix: Click Check for updates at the top right of the Updates list. If Photoshop still does not show, confirm your Mac runs macOS 14.0 or later, since 27.8 and 27.11 require it.

troubleshooting.problem: Tools such as Object Selection are missing after updating
troubleshooting.fix: Click and hold the three-dot button at the bottom of the toolbar, choose Restore Defaults, then click Done.

troubleshooting.problem: Photoshop behaves oddly or shows strange settings after the update
troubleshooting.fix: Export your presets first, then reset preferences by holding ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ while launching. The full steps are in the preferences reset guide linked above.

troubleshooting.problem: Photoshop stopped working after a macOS upgrade
troubleshooting.fix: Update through the Creative Cloud app to the current release. An Apple Community reply says v26.10 works on macOS 26.

troubleshooting.problem: You need an older build of Photoshop
troubleshooting.fix: Click the three-dot button to the left of Open, then choose Other Versions. The guide that describes this is from June 2020, so the menu may differ.
